title: Boston Climate Week Event: Companies Leading the Way on Climate Solutions
description: ​​Sustainserv is a Boston-based sustainability consulting firm with offices in Boston, Frankfurt, and Zurich. Boston-based companies have long been meaningfully engaged in sustainability efforts, and more recently, aggressive efforts to reduce their impacts on climate change. In the course of doing so, they have spear-headed innovative approaches to energy efficiency, circularity and creative approaches to financing sustainability efforts just to name a few. ​Join Sustainserv on May 7 at The Foundry in Cambridge for a session where some of the thought leaders of the Boston corporate sustainability scene discuss their efforts to combat climate change, talk about the challenges and opportunities, and to help chart the course forward in these dynamic times. ​A wine/beer reception will follow to cap off the session. ​SPEAKERS ​Cristina Mendoza, Sustainserv Director, will lead a panel with corporate Sustainability leaders including: ​ Julie Kae, Qlik Technologies ​Alyssa Caddle, Thermo Fisher ​Danielle Ricketts, Kindercare ​Clare Connolly, Eversource ​ ​This event is free entry with limited tickets available

title: Mount Auburn Hospital presents Pink Pages on June 8th at the American Repertory Theater
description: Join award-winning author and breast cancer survivor Alice Hoffman for an unforgettable evening of storytelling, connection, and purpose—benefiting the Hoffman Breast Center at Mount Auburn Hospital. This year’s featured guests include: Chris Bohjalian Meredith Goldstein Ann Leary Wally Lamb Jill McCorkle Liz Walker Emceed by Emmy Award-winning journalist Joyce Kulhawik. All proceeds benefit the Hoffman Breast Center at Mount Auburn Hospital, providing critical care, resources, and support for patients and families navigating breast cancer. title: C’port Textile & Book Drive, May 30
description: Please join the CNA on May 30th for our Textile & Book Drive, 10-2 in Hastings Sq Park. Whether you're behind on spring cleaning or interested in limiting what goes to the landfill, we have the solution for you! We've partnered with two organizations to responsibly recycle, reuse, or resell items. Please visit our website or the links below for additional info on accepted items & conditions for each: • Textiles will be sorted by Helpsy, who takes a wide variety of clothing, shoes, and household textiles in all conditions (broken, torn, stained, etc.). • Books will be resold by More Than Words, dedicated to empowering youth through job training. Here, quality matters (no heavy damage, mold, or missing pages). All info on items accepted, visit our website: https://www.cambridgeport.org/drive Interested in volunteering, or have tables/chairs/tarps to lend? Email Lexi via alexisbeckwith@gmail.com or fill out our CNA Volunteer Interest Form. Location Hastings Square, 321 Brookline St,

title: 5th Annual Juneteenth Gathering
description: Gather for Juneteenth to honor those who endured slavery and seized freedom on Brattle Street 250 years ago, their descendants, and the long history of Black freedom activism in Cambridge and beyond. This free, all-ages event is marking its fifth year in 2025! Denise Washington (#Pop-Up Poetry Series), a descendant of Darby Vassall, has curated the Juneteenth Gathering at Longfellow House-Washington's Headquarters NHS each year. Join us for the Juneteenth Gathering, A Denise Plays Hard Event, featuring poetry, music, historical displays, family activities, and refreshments. All are welcome! 4:00-5:00 pm Community partner tables, music, refreshments, and activities 5:00-7:00 pm Speakers and Juneteenth #Pop Up Poetry, A Denise Plays Hard Event
venue_name: Longfellow House-Washington's Headquarters National Historic Site

title: AI Fluency: A Hands-On Skills Intensive
description: Join The AI Collective Group and the Museum of Science for two hours of real, hands-on AI learning with expert instructors in person, at one of Boston's most trusted institutions, surrounded by people who showed up for the same reason you did. The AI Collective Group has guided over 200 students through in-person, hands-on AI learning. They know the material and they know how to make it land. This is not a webinar or a panel. It's a working lab so bring your laptop and your curiosity.

title: Reading is Sexy: A Smutty Comedy Show for Book Nerds
description: Join New Normal Comedy and All She Wrote Books for a night of smut and standup comedy! A lineup of Boston’s best and nerdiest comics who definitely think the book is better than the movie will be riffing about all things, smut, romance, and fan fic. The night will begin with an hour of private shopping for ticket holders and conclude with a 90-minute standup comedy show packed with romance hot takes and Heated Rivalry references. Content will be adult-themed and discretion is advised. A portion of ticket sales will be donated to LUCE to help keep our immigrant neighbors safe. This show is presented as part of Sex Week Boston. Show FAQs: Masks: Masks not required but not discouraged. New Normal requests that anyone with COVID or flu-like symptoms refrain from attending to protect vulnerable and immuno-compromised community members. Ticket Pricing: Tickets are $15 online and $20 at the door. Sliding scale and student pricing is available; please reach out to newnormalboston@gmail.com for more information. Accessibility: All She Wrote Books is wheelchair accessible. This event is presented by New Normal Comedy and All She Wrote Books as part of Sex Week Boston. About New Normal Comedy: New Normal Comedy is a Boston-based standup comedy collective that produces shows centering those who are historically underrepresented onstage: women, people of color, LGBTQIA+ folks, people with disabilities, etc. New Normal specializes in community-oriented shows and has partnered with local organizations like All She Wrote Books, Porter Square Books, Read My Lips, Dignity Matters, and Prison Book Program. New Normal shows aim to make the stage feel like home, to create a room where comics feel like they can succeed, and to bring people who haven’t been made to feel normal, together.
